To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can use MapReduce to incrementally load data into database systems, (2) we can use this technique to improve query performance, (3) the technique is robust to the presence of errors in the input data, (4) the technique is scalable to large data sets and large numbers of queries.

we have designed a system that allows data to be loaded into a database system in the same time as it is processed by MapReduce jobs over the file system, and that this system achieves a significant performance improvement for future queries.

(a) it is possible to piggyback data transfer operations on top of existing MapReduce operations, and that this piggybacking can be made invisible to the user, and (b) the resulting system can be used to load data into database systems in a way that allows for immediate gratification, and still provides the long-term performance and functionality benefits of database systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how can a database system be used as a "black box", without requiring any upfront effort?
how to leverage the MapReduce framework for the purpose of data loading and organization.
making the upfront effort of data transfer into a database system transparent, so that users may focus their efforts on modeling the data, and on writing queries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we are able to achieve the following: (a) a 2x to 4x speedup in query execution times, (b) a reduction in the time-to-first-query by a factor of 2 to 4, (c) a reduction in data movement by a factor of at least 4, and (d) an improvement in the overall system throughput by a factor of up to 2.

the proposed system is able to achieve the best of both worlds, i.e., it is capable of running queries over the data in the file system with the performance of the Hadoop framework while it is able to achieve significant performance improvements for future queries by transferring the data into an analytical database system.

our approach is a significant advance over prior approaches, in that it allows the use of a database system for the first time, without requiring a significant up front investment of time or resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our system allows users to run MapReduce jobs over raw files, while still making incremental progress towards loading the data into a database system.
we have built a new system, called H2O, which allows us to load and organize data into a database system in a way that is invisible to the user.
we have designed, implemented, and evaluated an end-to-end system for invisible loading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the upfront effort of data transfer and data preparation is a major bottleneck in the "time-to-first analysis", and we propose a system that can alleviate this problem.

the upfront effort of data transfer can be amortized across a large number of MapReduce jobs, and thus the performance benefits of database system can be realized incrementally, and in a cost-efficient manner.
it is possible to incrementally load data into database systems in a way that does not affect the latency of the original MapReduce jobs.
